title: Admissibility of integral compactification refinement diagrams
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness of the schemes is imposed. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories $C_s(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ [def-sf-categories], completed at integral stages and with positive finite levels $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\ge1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Fix $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$ and $A_n=R/t^n$. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$. Use their derived categories, the canonical reduction system $\mathcal R_W K$, exact termwise open extension $J_j$, and total derived system proper direct image $S_p$ [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. A system is normalized if every transition-adjoint $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible.

Let $K\in C_{R}(X)$ and suppose all its reductions have Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$. Choose an identity or binary compactification-refinement diagram for $f$, with quasi-compact open factors $j_c$, proper factors $p_c$ and proper refinements $u,v$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Consider every intermediate system obtained from $\mathcal R_XK$ along any of the finitely many words in $J_j,S_p$ in that diagram, including hidden open intermediates in $S_{p_c}J_{j_c}$ and the refinement proper images.

Every such intermediate system is normalized, has constructible levels with a common finite cohomological interval and a common finite Tor interval independent of $n$, and has bounded etale-origin witnesses compatible with its actual coefficient transitions. More precisely an open extension preserves a chosen Tor interval; a proper factor with source dimension bounded by $d\ge0$ sends $[a',b']$ into $[a',b'+2d]$. All sources have finite dimension, and $d=0$ is admissible for an empty source. A single common upper bound can be chosen for the finite collection of words. Each intermediate system is canonically identified, with its quotient transitions, with the reduction system of the corresponding derived-complete constructible integral intermediate object. These are the intermediate-domain conditions of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], so the realization isomorphisms $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] apply to this whole identity or binary refinement diagram.

proof.text: Consider all prefixes of the finitely many operation words, retaining the prefix $J_{j_c}$ inside each $S_{p_c}J_{j_c}$. Proper factors, including $u,v$, are separated and finite type by definition. Finite-type composition makes their ambient schemes finite type over $k$; the open intermediates in the supplied diagram are finite type as well. Apply the geometry lemma to their structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a one-point Noetherian scheme of dimension zero). Thus each source has finite dimension; choose a nonnegative bound $d_p$ for every proper factor. The geometry lemma allows empty sources, for which choose $d_p=0$. No absolute separatedness enters. We will induct on prefix length with invariant: normalization, levelwise constructibility, a level-independent Tor interval $[a,B]$, and compatible bounded etale origins. Testing Tor amplitude on the coefficient sheaf itself also gives the cohomological interval $[a,B]$.

proof.text: Here is the origin procedure used at every prefix. For a normalized system $M$ with constructible levels and common cohomological interval, the finite-ring origin equivalence gives bounded constructible witnesses $\alpha_n:\nu^*L_n\cong M_n$, in that same interval. Apply the normalized-origin-witness theorem to its actual transition adjoints $\rho_{m,n}$. It supplies unique $\beta_{m,n}:L_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\cong L_n$ satisfying $\alpha_n\nu^*\beta_{m,n}=\rho_{m,n}(\alpha_m\otimes^LA_n)$, and the quotient cocycle. Consequently the witnesses respect the actual transitions, rather than a separately chosen tower. In particular each $L_m\otimes^LA_n$ is bounded below. At the empty prefix, $M=\mathcal R_XK$ is normalized by actual reconstruction; constructibility follows from the integral category hypothesis, and the assumed Tor interval $[a,b]$ gives common cohomological interval $[a,b]$. The procedure therefore establishes the full induction invariant initially.

source.place: Tag 09B1, lemma-compare-derived (2); the finite-ring origin and normalized-witness DAG statements specify the constructible, coefficient-compatible refinements. Initial normalization uses the actual-reconstruction statement.

proof.text:
Suppose the invariant holds for $M$ on the source of an open factor $j$, with Tor interval $[a,B]$. Exact termwise extension evaluates to $(J_jM)_n=j_!M_n$. The open-ctf lemma gives constructibility and the same Tor and cohomological intervals at every level. The canonical open tensor/coefficient isomorphism identifies the transition-adjoint for the actual extended transition with
$$(j_!M_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\xrightarrow{j_!\rho_{m,n}}j_!M_n.$$
Both arrows are invertible. This is the coefficient-ring specialization of the open base-change/tensor comparison, which is natural also on strict ringed diagram sites. Thus $J_jM$ is normalized for its given transitions. The origin procedure of step 2 now supplies compatible bounded witnesses for $J_jM$. This also verifies every hidden open prefix of a compact-support constructor.

proof.text: For a proper factor $p:V\to W$, derived system evaluation identifies $(S_pM)_n$ with $Rp_{*,n}M_n$, including the actual coefficient-restriction transitions. Applying the direct-image-ctf theorem to each $M_n$ gives constructibility and Tor interval $[a,B+2d_p]$, hence cohomology in that interval. For $m\ge n$, put $A=A_m$, $B'=A_n$. The origins supplied in step 2 satisfy $L_m\in D^+$ and $L_m\otimes_A^LB'\cong L_n\in D^+$; these are precisely the bounded-origin hypotheses of proper scalar comparison. Its canonical $B'$-linear counit mate $\chi$ is therefore invertible, without any flatness assumption on $A\to B'$.

proof.text:
The adjoint of the actual transition of $S_pM$ is
$$(Rp_{*,m}M_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\chi}Rp_{*,n}(M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\xrightarrow{Rp_{*,n}(\rho_{m,n})}Rp_{*,n}M_n.$$
Indeed the scalar adjoint of this composite is $Rp_{*,m}$ of $M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n$, followed by the restriction-of-scalars comparison: substitute the defining counit equation for $\chi$, then the tensor/restriction adjunction equation for $\rho_{m,n}$. These are the evaluated transitions specified by the derived system comparison. Both displayed arrows are isomorphisms by step 4 and normalization of $M$. Hence $S_pM$ is normalized with its actual quotient maps. The cocycle is already the cocycle of those transitions; no new transitions are chosen. Apply the origin procedure of step 2 to obtain compatible bounded origins for this output. This proves the proper induction step, including refinement images under $u,v$.

proof.text: Induction on the nonnegative prefix length now applies steps 3 and 4–5 to every constructor. More explicitly assign $B_{\varnothing}=b$, $B_{J_jV}=B_V$, and $B_{S_pV}=B_V+2d_p$. Every prefix has the asserted properties with interval $[a,B_V]$, independently of $n$. The set of prefixes is finite and nonempty (it contains the empty word), so $B_{\max}=\max_V B_V$ exists; $[a,B_{\max}]$ simultaneously bounds Tor and cohomology for the entire diagram. Identity refinements add no cost beyond the permissible proper estimate, and zero objects on empty sources satisfy all these containments. This is an induction over finite syntax, with its base proved in step 2 and both successor cases proved above.

proof.text:
All intermediate-system conditions in the expression-domain definition now hold for every word, including its hidden open prefixes. The inputs are derived-complete constructible integral objects by hypothesis. Thus the conditional realization theorem applies and gives its specified $c_V:\mathcal L M_V\cong V_{\rm int}(K)$, with $M_V=V(\mathcal R_XK)$. Independently, actual reconstruction gives a complete $\mathcal L M_V$ and the isomorphism of strict derived systems $e_{M_V}:\mathcal R\mathcal L M_V\cong M_V$. The required identification is the actual composite
$$\mathcal R(V_{\rm int}(K))\xrightarrow{\mathcal R(c_V^{-1})}\mathcal R\mathcal L M_V\xrightarrow{e_{M_V}}M_V.$$
It respects all quotient transitions because both factors are whole-system morphisms. The realized object is complete, and its reductions have the constructibility and common bounds just proved, so the integral constructibility definition puts it in $C_R$. This proves the claimed identification with the corresponding integral intermediate and the applicability of all $c_V$ throughout the refinement diagram.
